tagline.en: Home park, Amish neighbors, and the valley table — mapped from Buhl Park.

greeting.en: Welcome home. I'm David — walk with me from Buhl Park to the Amish roads and the valley's favorite tables.

en.heroLine: Buhl Park at the center — Amish countryside nearby, and the local plates that taste like home.

copy.en: In the heart of the Shenango Valley, Buhl Park's 270 acres hold trails, Lake Julia, free nine-hole golf, and the gatherings that stitch Hermitage and Sharon together.

narration.en: Start at Buhl Park — the valley's shared front yard since nineteen fifteen.

copy.en: Luigi's has been serving pie in Hermitage since 1955. Quaker Steak & Lube opened the original motor-themed wing house in Sharon in 1974 — both still define the valley table.

narration.en: Two tables for now — Luigi's pizza and the original Quaker Steak and Lube.

copy.en: Around New Wilmington, Old Order Amish farms stretch across Lawrence and Mercer counties — brown-topped buggies, quiet roads, and markets that ask for courtesy over spectacle.

narration.en: Just south-east of Buhl Park, New Wilmington anchors the local Amish countryside — not Lancaster.

blurb.en: 270-acre heart of the Shenango Valley — trails, Lake Julia, recreation, and free nine-hole golf since 1915.
Western Pennsylvania's Old Order Amish settlement — farms around New Wilmington and Volant, roughly ten miles from Buhl Park.
The original Quaker Steak & Lube opened in 1974 in a former service station — motor-themed wings and a Sharon landmark.
Shenango Valley pizza institution since 1955 — often voted Best of the Best by local readers.

history.en: Born in a vacant auto service station on Chestnut Street, the Sharon Lube invented the motor-garage dining vibe and put Shenango Valley wings on the national map. Bike Night, sauces by the dozen, and the original address still matter.
A neighborhood pizzeria on East State Street that has fed the valley for generations. Classic pies, local loyalty, and the kind of counter where everyone already knows your order.

Share the road with buggies, keep cameras pointed at barns and fields — never at people without clear permission — and buy from roadside stands when they are open. The countryside around New Wilmington is a living community.
